Try a weighted combination on the full pool using inverse_error weights to exploit the strong leading model ETS while remaining robust to ranking instability.
Use a smaller, trend‑focused pool (pool1) and weight by inverse error to test if a lightweight weighted combo beats the current leader.
Test a robust trimmed‑mean on the full model pool to see if trimming improves over simple mean and weighted schemes for this trend‑dominated series.
try a weighted combination on the full pool using handle w1 to see if different weighting improves over the current leader.
The series is trend‑dominated with unstable ranking; a robust median over a small, high‑ranking pool may help reduce outlier influence.
try a robust dba combination on the full pool to see if iterative refinement improves over the weighted leader (trend-dominated, robust hint).
Test a simple mean on the restricted stable pool1 to see if fewer models reduce variance.
Test a weighted combination on pool2 using inverse_error to see if adding FT_rf improves robustness in this trend-dominated, unstable ranking series.
test a robust DBA combination on the smaller stable pool1, hoping to reduce variance in this trend-dominated, unstable ranking series.
Try a weighted combination on the larger but still stable pool3, using inverse_error to exploit the strong trend and moderate seasonality while reducing variance from correlated models.

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted weighted by w1' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9827. Series context: trend strength 0.7635 and seasonal strength 0.3287; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.119); 3 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.375.
